## Mass-fraction state and its mixture totals (`ThermoY`) {#sec-ch03-thermo-y}

### Summary

A dynamical core advances density, internal energy and the mass fractions of the tracers, so its natural
thermodynamic state is $(\rho, U, y)$. `ThermoY` works on that state. It converts mass fractions to partial
densities and mole fractions, and computes pressure, temperature, heat capacity, internal energy and entropy per
unit volume. Its `forward` method, the saturation adjustment at fixed energy and volume, is the subject of
@sec-ch04.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Conversions of the $(\rho, U, y)$ state; the mixture totals @eq-ch03-thermo-y-totals.

**Data.** $\rho$ [kg m$^{-3}$], $U$ [J m$^{-3}$], $y_n$ [-] for $n \ge 1$ (dry implicit), partial densities
$\rho_n$ [kg m$^{-3}$].

**Placement.** Called by the host's equation of state and before and after saturation adjustment.

**Activation.** API: `ThermoY(options)`, then `compute("<from>-><to>", [...])`.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact except `VU->T` and `PV->T`, Newton iterations to `ftol` within `max_iter`.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer.
:::

Symbols of the notation table (@sec-appa): $y_n$, mass fraction [-]; $\rho_n$, partial density [kg m$^{-3}$]; $\rho$, total
density [kg m$^{-3}$]; $U$, internal energy [J m$^{-3}$] and $C_V$, heat capacity at constant volume
[J m$^{-3}$ K$^{-1}$], both per unit volume; $c_n$, $x_n$, $N_{\mathrm g}$ as in @sec-ch03-eos. Local symbols:
$\mu_n$, molar mass [kg mol$^{-1}$]; $S$, entropy per unit volume [J m$^{-3}$ K$^{-1}$].

The `compute` keys are named by their inputs and output: `V` is the vector of partial densities $\rho_n$ (the
code's "inverse specific volume", `ivol`), `D` the density, `Y` the mass fractions, `X` the mole fractions.

### Derivation

**Partial densities and concentrations.** Species 0 is the dry gas and carries no mass fraction of its own:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\rho_0 &= \rho \left(1 - \sum_{n \ge 1} y_n\right), \\
\rho_n &= \rho\, y_n, \quad n \ge 1, \\
c_n &= \rho_n / \mu_n .
\end{aligned}
$$

`DY->V` computes the first two lines, `V->Y` inverts them with $y_n = \rho_n / \sum_k \rho_k$.

**Mole fractions.** With $y_0 = 1 - \sum_{n\ge1} y_n$, the mole fraction is
$x_n = (y_n/\mu_n) / \sum_k (y_k/\mu_k)$. Multiply numerator and denominator by $\mu_0$ and write the $k = 0$ term
out:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mu_0 \sum_k \frac{y_k}{\mu_k} &= 1 - \sum_{k \ge 1} y_k + \sum_{k\ge1} y_k \frac{\mu_0}{\mu_k}
= 1 + \sum_{k\ge1} y_k \left(\frac{\mu_0}{\mu_k} - 1\right) , \\
x_n &= \frac{y_n\, \mu_0/\mu_n}{1 + \sum_{k\ge1} y_k \left(\mu_0/\mu_k - 1\right)}, \quad n \ge 1 .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch03-thermo-y-xfrac}

and $x_0 = 1 - \sum_{n\ge1} x_n$. @eq-ch03-thermo-y-xfrac is computed in `_yfrac_to_xfrac`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::_yfrac_to_xfrac >}}).

**Mixture totals.** Each total is a concentration-weighted sum of the per-species functions of
@sec-ch03-species-functions:

$$
\begin{aligned}
U &= \sum_n c_n u_n(T), \\
C_V &= \sum_n c_n c_{v,n}(T), \\
S &= \sum_n c_n s_n(T, p) .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch03-thermo-y-totals}

The first line is computed in `_intEng_vol` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo.hpp ThermoYImpl::_intEng_vol >}}), the
second in `_cv_vol` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::_cv_vol >}}), the third in `_entropy_vol`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo.hpp ThermoYImpl::_entropy_vol >}}), which uses the condensate entropy of
@eq-ch03-species-functions-scond. `TUS->F` returns the Helmholtz energy $U - T S$.

**Temperature from energy.** `VU->T` solves $U(T) = U_{\mathrm{given}}$ for $T$. Since $\mathrm d U/\mathrm d T =
C_V$, Newton's method is

$$
T \leftarrow T + \frac{U_{\mathrm{given}} - \sum_n c_n u_n(T)}{\sum_n c_n c_{v,n}(T)} ,
$$ {#eq-ch03-thermo-y-newton}

started from the constant-heat-capacity solution $T = (U_{\mathrm{given}} - \sum_n \rho_n u_{0,n}) / \sum_n \rho_n
c_{v0,n}$, where $u_{0,n}$ [J kg$^{-1}$] and $c_{v0,n}$ [J kg$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$] are the energy offset at $T = 0$ and
the constant heat capacity per unit mass. With no extra functions and no NASA-9 or H$_2$ option, $U$ is linear in
$T$ and the start is exact. @eq-ch03-thermo-y-newton is computed in `_intEng_to_temp`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::_intEng_to_temp >}}).

Why the start is exact: with constant heat capacities $U = \sum_n \rho_n (u_{0,n} + c_{v0,n} T)$ is linear in $T$,
and the start is the root of that line. Newton's slope is the exact $\mathrm d U/\mathrm d T = C_V$, so with the
NASA-9 or H$_2$ option, where $U$ is curved, the iteration converges quadratically from that start.

**One energy model for the conversion and the saturation adjustment.** The saturation adjustment at fixed
$(\rho, U)$ (@sec-ch04) must release latent heat and set $T$ with the same $u_n(T)$ that `VU->T` inverts. Otherwise
a parcel adjusted to saturation and then converted back with `VU->T` sits off its saturation curve. At the pin the
kernel receives the constant-$c_v$ offsets even under `use-h2-cp` (`ThermoYImpl::forward`,
{{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::forward >}}): the defect D12, whose fix gives the kernel the H2
rotational energy (@sec-ch03-reference-state).[^ch03-thermo-y-d12]

### Numerical method

Every conversion is pointwise. The two iterations, `VU->T` (@eq-ch03-thermo-y-newton) and `PV->T`
(@sec-ch03-eos), stop when the largest relative temperature change over all cells,
$\max \lvert 1 - T_{\mathrm{old}}/T_{\mathrm{new}} \rvert$, is below `ftol` (default $10^{-6}$), or after `max_iter`
iterations (default 10). The test is global: one slow cell keeps every cell iterating, and each test copies one
value to the host. Both keys are set in YAML under `dynamics: equation-of-state:` as `ftol` and `max-iter`.

Tensor layout: mass fractions are `(ny, ...)` with the species first, partial densities and mole fractions are
`(..., 1 + ny)` with the species last, where `ny` is the number of species minus one.

The `ThermoY` figure is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| module | {{< code src/thermo/thermo.hpp ThermoYImpl >}} | `ThermoYImpl` | API |
| dispatch of conversions | {{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::compute >}} | `compute` | key string |
| `DY->V` | {{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::_yfrac_to_ivol >}} | `_yfrac_to_ivol` | always |
| `V->Y` | {{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::_ivol_to_yfrac >}} | `_ivol_to_yfrac` | always |

| `VT->U` | {{< code src/thermo/thermo.hpp ThermoYImpl::_intEng_vol >}} | `_intEng_vol` | always |
| `VU->T` | {{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::_intEng_to_temp >}} | `_intEng_to_temp` | `ftol`, `max-iter` |
| `VT->cv` | {{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::_cv_vol >}} | `_cv_vol` | always |
| `PVT->S` | {{< code src/thermo/thermo.hpp ThermoYImpl::_entropy_vol >}} | `_entropy_vol` | always |

: Code map of `ThermoY`. {#tbl-ch03-thermo-y-code}

Setup checks and warnings a user can hit: `V->Y`, `Y->X` and `DY->V` refuse an input whose species count is not
the module's ("mass fraction size mismatch"); an unknown key is refused ("Unknown abbreviation"); `VU->T` and
`PV->T` warn when `max_iter` is reached and return the last iterate.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_thermo.release` (`DeviceTest.thermo_y`) | `DY->V` then `V->Y` returns $y$ | $10^{-4}$ rel. and abs. | not yet derived |
| `test_thermo.release` (`DeviceTest.thermo_y`) | `VT->U` then `VU->T` returns $T$ | $10^{-4}$ rel. and abs. | not yet derived |
| `test_thermo.release` (`DeviceTest.thermo_yx`) | `Y->X` then `X->Y` returns $y$ | $10^{-4}$ rel. and abs. | not yet derived |
| `test_thermo.release` (`DeviceTest.eng_pres`) | `VU->T` returns the $T$ of a `ThermoX` state | $10^{-4}$ rel. and abs. | not yet derived |

: Tests of `ThermoY`. {#tbl-ch03-thermo-y-tests}

The tolerances are read from `tests/test_thermo.cpp` at the pin; they are much looser than the float64 round-off of
these conversions, and their reason is missing evidence. The cases run on CPU in float32 and float64 and on CUDA
when a GPU is present. `PVT->S` is computed but not asserted in `DeviceTest.thermo_y`.

The derivation is checked by `check_ch3_thermo_y.py`:[^ch03-thermo-y-check]

- `(d1)`: `Y->X` against @eq-ch03-thermo-y-xfrac on `tests/jupiter.yaml` with random mass fractions, to
  $2.2 \times 10^{-19}$ (tolerance $10^{-14}$).
- `(d2)`: `VT->U` then `VU->T` returns $T$ exactly (0 against $10^{-10}$ K) at 150-400 K with constant $c_v$.
- `(d3)`: the same round trip with `use-h2-cp`, both modes, to $3.7 \times 10^{-12}$ K.
- `(d4)`: a supersaturated H2 + H2O parcel adjusted at fixed $(\rho, U)$ by `ThermoY.forward` and converted back with
  `VU->T`. With the flag off it ends on the saturation curve,
  $\lvert \ln p_{\mathrm v} - \ln K(T)\rvert = 9.2 \times 10^{-7}$
  (tolerance $10^{-5}$). With `use-h2-cp` it ends $4.6 \times 10^{-3}$ off the curve in both modes, EXPECTED-FAIL
  (D12).

### Limits

The convergence test is a global maximum with a host copy per iteration, which serialises GPU work (a performance
hypothesis, not measured). With `use-h2-cp` the round trip itself is exact (check line `(d3)`), but at the pin the
saturation adjustment uses a different energy model and ends off the curve (D12, check line `(d4)`).
